article.title: Decline of the American Empire
article.author: Tom Engelhardt
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Talk about extreme. Talk about mad. Talk about off the charts. We’re all now, I fear, on the national equivalent of the Six Flags roller coaster from which a man recently fell to his death . Honestly, can you even believe this world of ours? This old guy can’t, I’ll tell you that. Nothing truly prepared me for Donald J. Trump as president of the United States—not once, but twice!—or for the all-too-bizarre world that came with him. (Or did it, in fact, arrive ahead of him and pave the way?) How could I ever have prepared myself for that? I mean, great imperial powers have gone down many, many times before in history, but not, I suspect, quite this way, not by giving that downhill slide the imprint and imprimatur of a genuine maniac as imperial leader. Not by implementing that roller-coaster-style ride with a full-scale nuttiness that, once upon a time, would have been politically beyond imagining in this country. Go ahead, give me another example of such a phenomenon, of a leader like Trump in the history of any great power in decline (and there have certainly been many of those). Personally, I can’t think of one in the last couple of centuries ever being headed by quite the equivalent of You Know Who at just such a moment. And yet, strangely enough, I’ve seen no one say such a thing. Related: Welcome to Trumpworld, Where Political Reality Defies Belief Keep in mind, of course, that Donald Trump is all too emblematic of this world of... well, I’m not sure I can say “ours” anymore. In a way, symbolically speaking, you couldn’t ask for anything more descriptive of our moment than him and the way he’s rejected outright the all-too-obvious state of a planet also going down, down, down in roller-coaster fashion, not if you want to truly grasp what’s happening in this world of ours these days. As he said at the United Nations in 2025, “This ‘climate change,’ it’s the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world, in my opinion. All of these predictions made by the United Nations and many others, often for bad reasons, were wrong. They were made by stupid people that have cost their countries fortunes and given those same countries no chance for success. If you don’t get away from this green scam, your country is going to fail.” Buy the Book Yes, the president of the United States, a remarkable scamster himself, has simply rejected reality as a scam in a way that should be considered historically remarkable, if not unique. Having first done so long ago (calling climate change a Chinese “hoax” as early as 2012), he’s never really stopped. And little harm it did him, it seems. After all, on this distinctly warming planet of ours, he did indeed win a second term in office in 2024. Of course, when the British Empire (or, in fact, any other great imperial power of the past that you want to mention) went down, our planet wasn’t yet on the downhill slope as well. Now, however, it certainly is. (Hey, it’s early November and, here in a distinctly warming New York City , I have yet to don my usual fall jacket even once!) So, perhaps as the leader of what remains the greatest power (or possibly I mean greatest mess of a power) on this planet, Donald Trump will come to be known not as the “hot” president but as the heat president (as he’s making our all-American world ever hotter, whether you’re talking about politics or the weather). He’s even agreed to pay companies to cancel planned wind-power projects And speaking about the (political) weather, it’s true that American voters only recently rejected him in what’s come to be known as a “ blue tsunami “ (though maybe a red Trumpnami would have been more accurate). Still, whatever we voters did in the recent midterm elections, the mad Donald distinctly remains the president of the United States for two more incredible (or do I mean incredulous?) years and that certainly is no small thing. And only recently, he also appointed Stephen Miller as his chief of staff. Yes, we’re talking about the fellow that Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has termed “a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands.” Related: Climate Change Is a Slow-Motion Nuclear War—and We're Already Counting the Dead A Trumpian Heat Tsunami In some fashion, given the recent election, Donald Trump does distinctly seem to be going down, down, down. Unfortunately, he also seems remarkably prepared to do his best in the two years to come to take the rest of us and the planet down with him. And believe me, that’s no small thing. After all, American voters have twice elected a climate-change denier of the first order to the highest office not just in the land but, given American power, in the world. And if you don’t think that’s remarkable, historically (or do I mean futuristically?) speaking, then I wonder what is? Yes, it’s all too obvious that this planet is now going down, down, down, thanks to the continued pouring of fossil fuels into the atmosphere and the distinct overheating of this world of ours. And it’s not exactly complicated what needs to be done in response. Nonharmful energy sources (solar, wind, and hydropower) have to become the heart and soul of human life on this planet. But don’t even dream of such a thing in the universe of Donald J. Trump, who seems intent on nothing less than taking us all (and our children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren) down with him in what might be thought of as a Trumpian heat tsunami. At the very least, in imperial terms, he’s turning climate change (and so the fate of this planet) over to that other great power of this moment, the rising green power and largest investor in green energy on this planet, China (even if that country also continues to pour more fossil fuels— 35% of the global total —into the atmosphere than any other country). In the meantime, give him the credit he deserves. After all, he is president for the second time of the imperial power that, since World War II, has put more money into its military than so many other countries combined. A possible $1.5 trillion is likely to go into the Pentagon budget alone in 2027 and President Trump has never really stopped fighting (and losing ) wars against far lesser powers. In doing so, he is, believe it or not, following in a great American tradition with the war he launched (with Israel) against Iran that has proven (with the Strait of Hormuz closed ) a global economic catastrophe and undoubtedly helped the Democrats sweep the recent midterm elections. Related: Donald Trump: The President of American Decline For Donald Trump, it seems that there are simply never enough tsunamis on this misbegotten planet of ours and he’s continued to threaten far worse in his war with Iran, saying that he may have to “destroy the rest of the country” (which might, of course, even be a threat, for the first time in more than 80 years, to use atomic weaponry on this planet, though he’s also denied that he would do so). Can there be any question that, two years into his second term in office, he is now taking us (and the rest of the planet) on a roller coaster ride to hell, or do I mean into the trashcan of history? It makes this 82-year-old grandfather sad indeed to imagine the world that “my” president is now preparing (if that’s faintly the word for it) for my grandchildren. They just don’t deserve this, do they? Tom's Substack
